ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** Both sections cover the recap of previous lessons, the transition to multimodality, and why text-only systems fail on visually-rich content. The generated section names financial reports, medical diagnostics, and building sketches directly, covering all three of the expected section's named limitation examples plus technical diagrams as a complementary addition; only 'research assistants' from the guideline's fuller list is absent, and that specific item is not named in the expected section either, so it is not a CoreContent gap.

Limitations of Traditional Document Processing:
**1:** Both sections cover the OCR pipeline, the rigid/fragile/costly framing, cascading errors, and specific failure-mode statistics, and both name building sketches/nested tables as complex-layout examples. All substantive ideas present in the expected section are present here.

Foundations of Multimodal LLMs:
**1:** Both sections explain the two architectures, image encoders (all three: CLIP, OpenCLIP, SigLIP), embedding alignment, the 2025 model landscape, modality extension, and the diffusion distinction. Model-list coverage is thinner than the expected section's four named open-source models (only Llama 4 and Qwen3 are named here, vs. the expected section's Llama 4/Gemma 2/Qwen3/DeepSeek R1-V3), but the core comparative point -- open-weight models now rival closed ones -- is preserved; flagged as borderline given two of four named models are dropped this time, more than the single-item thinning seen in other replicates.

Applying Multimodal LLMs to Images and PDFs:
**1:** Both sections cover raw bytes, Base64, public URLs, private-data-lake URLs (now with the actual mocked GCS code example, unlike the immediately preceding replicate), the two-image comparison demonstration (also restored here), object detection, and the parallel PDF treatment. No substantive idea from the expected section is absent this time.

Foundations of Multimodal RAG:
**0:** Both sections cover the generic RAG architecture, ColPali's OCR-bypassing role, the bag-of-embeddings representation, and the ViDoRe 81.3% figure. Unlike every prior replicate graded so far, this section explicitly states ColPali's PaliGemma/SigLIP model composition -- closing half of the recurring three-article gap. However, the GitHub repository reference ('illuin-tech/colpali'), also explicit in the expected section, is still absent.

Implementing Multimodal RAG for Images, PDFs and Text:
**1:** Both sections cover the image grid, create_vector_index with its aside about the embedding workaround, the helper functions, search_multimodal, both example queries, and -- unlike the immediately preceding replicate -- a closing synthesis statement about the unified index extending across modalities. The one gap is a missing demonstration of the vector_index's keys/first-element content, a single minor omission rather than a pattern of them.

Building Multimodal AI Agents:
**1:** Both sections cover the ways multimodal capability is added to agents, wrapping the RAG function as a tool, building the ReAct agent, and the kitten-color question through to the final answer. As in every replicate graded so far, the expected section's Figure 23 (ReAct agent architecture image) has no counterpart, but this is a Flow matter, not a CoreContent one.

Conclusion:
**0:** Both sections frame the lesson as the close of Part 1 and recap the course arc. However, the expected section's specific claim -- that the Part 2 capstone's research agent will handle multimodal data (PDFs, images) and pass it to the writer agent -- is absent here; the generated section previews Part 2 only as 'we will apply these skills to build a complete research and writing agent system from scratch' with no mention of multimodality in that connection. This mirrors the gap found in one of the two prior-preset replicates and is the section's one substantive miss.

References:
**1:** Both sections contain a numbered list of references serving the same bibliographic purpose.
